Spread leans as a group did not beat the closing line in testing; only a spread lean in a proven tier can rate 7+ and count as a pick.

daily.headline: TCU wins 71% of 5,000 simulated games; favorites the model gave 70%–80% won 77% of 1,270 past games.

sections.title: The pick
lines: TCU to win outright: 71% of 5,000 simulated games.
Best price -220 at FanDuel, which implies 69%. A favorite this big pays little: $100 returns 45 in profit.
In testing (1,270 games where the model gave the underdog 20%–30%), the favorite won 77%; the model had said 75%.
Moneyline favorites are a likely win, not a proven money-maker: the betting edge The Lab found in testing is on underdogs and totals.

sections.title: The short answer
lines: The model favors TCU by 7.3 (Kansas 19.4, TCU 27.3); TCU wins 71% of 5,000 simulated games.
The books agree: TCU -6. The model likes TCU by 1.3 more than the line, which is why it leans TCU against the spread.
Best bet in this game: TCU over 25.5, rated 6.9 out of 10 (not a pick: picks need 7+).

sections.title: Why TCU is favored
lines: TCU has the better expected number in 5 of 6 parts of the game, opponent-adjusted and refit before this week (the last two seasons count most).
Expected points in this game: Kansas 17.5, TCU 27.2 (TCU by 9.7 points).
Expected EPA per play (garbage time out): Kansas +0.03, TCU −0.08 (Kansas by 0.11 EPA per play).
Expected success rate: Kansas 38%, TCU 39% (TCU by 2 points of success rate).
Expected yards per play: Kansas 4.84, TCU 6.02 (TCU by 1.18 yards per play).
Expected explosive-play rate: Kansas 6.9%, TCU 7.1% (TCU by 0.2 points of explosive rate).
Expected turnovers (fewer is better): Kansas 1.44, TCU 1.21 (TCU by 0.23 turnovers).
Expected plays (tempo): Kansas 65, TCU 66 (TCU runs 2 plays more).
TCU is at home (Amon G. Carter Stadium); home field is part of the rating fit.

sections.title: Season so far

sections.title: Track record behind the rating
lines: Team total leans in the Strong tier: 5,128 past games, won 52.9% (53.8% in 2025-2026, 1,347 games); break-even at -110 is 52.4%.
That tier beat the price on seasons the model never saw, so it counts as proven.
Every past team total bet rated 5–7: 3,057 graded, won 51.4%, returned −1.9¢ per $1 (−4.5¢ per $1 in recent seasons).

The rating ranks this bet's expected return (the calibrated chance at the best price) against every lean in the backtest: 8 means better than 80% of them. 7+ is the band that beat the books on seasons the model never saw.

sections.title: The upset case for Kansas
lines: Kansas wins 29% of the simulations; the moneyline (+195) implies 33% once the book's cut is removed. The model is lower on the upset by 4 points.
When the model gave an underdog 20–30%, those dogs really won 23.1% (1,270 games; the market had them at 23.8%).
Where Kansas rates better: epa per play.
In past games with a 2.5+ point underdog, the dogs that won better epa per play 73% of the time (13% when they lost), and better success rate 58% of the time (15% when they lost).
It is not a pick: the gap is not in the tier that made money in testing.

sections.title: What could go wrong
lines: Kansas still wins 29% of the 5,000 simulated games.
The middle 80% of simulated margins runs from Kansas by 11 to TCU by 27, so either team winning is a normal result.
Even the best bet here wins about 54% of the time, so it loses about 46%: a small edge that needs many bets to show up.
Spread leans as a group did not beat the closing line in testing; only a spread lean in a proven tier can rate 7+ and count as a pick.
